qt: to the Council Fabio Massimo Castaldo (Renew), Karin Karlsbro (Renew), Javier Nart (Renew), Karen Melchior (Renew), María Soraya Rodríguez Ramos (Renew), Bernard Guetta (Renew), Andrus Ansip (Renew) Subject:

As of 5 March 2025, over 4 300 000 residence permits, issued by various EU Member States through the Temporary Protection Directive to Ukrainian individuals fleeing Russia’s criminal invasion, are set to expire simultaneously, without any automatic renewal envisaged. Moreover, given the current situation in Ukraine and the prospect of a protracted conflict, it is evident that considerable time will be needed to ensure the safety of entire regions littered with mines, unexploded ordnance, and the reconstruction of entire urban centres and infrastructure such as roads and railway networks. 1.

Given the urgency and scale of this issue, is the Council launching any negotiations among the Member States with a view to extending the application of the Temporary Protection Directive to – at least – 5 March 2026?

Is the Council considering proposing that it be possible to extend these residence permits indefinitely, taking a joint approach among the Member States, until the situation in Ukraine allows for the safe return of displaced individuals to their territories, including those who were living in regions illegally occupied by Russia?
at: (English version) to the Council Fabio Massimo Castaldo (Renew), Karin Karlsbro (Renew), Javier Nart (Renew), Karen Melchior (Renew), María Soraya Rodríguez Ramos (Renew), Bernard Guetta (Renew), Andrus Ansip (Renew) (12 March 2024) Subject: Urgent need to extend the Temporary Protection Directive for Ukrainian refugees fleeing the Russian invasion As of 5 March 2025, over 4 300 000 residence permits, issued by various EU Member States through the Temporary Protection Directive to Ukrainian individuals fleeing Russia’s criminal invasion, are set to expire simultaneously, without any automatic renewal envisaged. Moreover, given the current situation in Ukraine and the prospect of a protracted conflict, it is evident that considerable time will be needed to ensure the safety of entire regions littered with mines, unexploded ordnance, and the reconstruction of entire urban centres and infrastructure such as roads and railway networks. 1. Given the urgency and scale of this issue, is the Council launching any negotiations among the Member States with a view to extending the application of the Temporary Protection Directive to — at least — 5 March 2026? 2. Is the Council considering proposing that it be possible to extend these residence permits indefinitely, taking a joint approach among the Member States, until the situation in Ukraine allows for the safe return of displaced individuals to their territories, including those who were living in regions illegally occupied by Russia? Reply (18 November 2024) On 25 June 2024 the Council adopted the Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/1836 extending temporary protection as introduced by Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/382 thereby temporary protection is extended until 4 March 2026. Regarding the Honourable Members’ second question on the possibility to extend these residence permits indefinitely, the Council recalls that Article 4(2) of Directive 2001/55/EC states that the Council may decide by qualified majority, on a proposal from the Commission, to extend temporary protection by up to one year where reasons for temporary protection persist.
